assumptions: Clip ground speeds were measured offline (Node FK) from the source clips, not by a browser foot-contact check; the Hips-dropped number was used for config. QA should still judge foot sliding visually.
Avatar-scale factor 1.03 (audit height ratio 1.865/1.809) applied to measured speeds for config clipSpeed.

Walk speed 1.6 m/s is slower than the spec default 2.2 m/s; it is the price of keeping the 1.0 m/s Mixamo walk within the 0.75 to 1.8 playback clamp. A faster walk clip would allow a higher walk speed (owner decision).
Shadows are off in M1 (QUALITY.low is used) because renderer shadow setup belongs to M5; resolveQuality exists but is not wired.
The Mixamo and Avaturn license statements in ASSETS.md are background knowledge, not a reading of current terms.

In dev with React Strict Mode the Physics provider frees and recreates its world between effect passes; colliders and motor dispose are try/catch tolerant of an already released world. This path was not exercised in a browser (production build only).

A404-free clip loading: only clips in FIRST_PLAY_CLIPS (walk, run) are requested. When idle, jump, fall and land are supplied, add their names to that list in config.ts and run npm run strip-clips; nothing else changes.
decisionsProposed: R1: tune locomotion speeds to the clips instead of re-sourcing: MOVEMENT.walkSpeed 1.6 and runSpeed 3.8 (spec 2.2 and 4.8), ANIMATION.clipSpeed walk 0.98 and run 2.93, timeScale clamp kept at 0.75 to 1.8 (resulting rates 1.63 and 1.30). Record as an addendum to ADR-003.

Rapier autostep workaround: the motor probes with a 0.06 m horizontal movement when a grounded step is blocked and keeps the result only if it stepped up (STEP_PROBE in player.ts). Without it walking at 1.6 m/s stalls against a 0.2 m step for about 2.5 s (measured).
Do not zero horizontal velocity on a blocked step; the controller needs the full desired movement each step for sliding and autostep.
MotorState.airTime is preserved through the landing step (reset on the next grounded step) so the animator can choose land versus soft landing.
strip-clips trims the duplicated last key only when every track ends on its first value; the first key sits at 1/30 s, so trimming yields the true loop period (41 and 22 frames).
Add @types/node ^22 (vitest peer) and an npm script strip-clips; keep vite-tsconfig-paths as designed even though Vite now supports tsconfig paths natively.
Selector /?arena=test is implemented in the shell (readLayoutParam); DEFAULT_LAYOUT is test-arena until CAMPUS exists in M3.

A minimal class error boundary in GameScene reports Physics/WASM failures to the loader so the hero is not broken (the design assigned this to M2; pulled forward because a WASM init failure would otherwise white-screen the canvas).
lessonsProposed: Validate generated glTF assets by parsing them with the runtime loader (GLTFLoader) in a test, not only by inspecting JSON structure: a strip-script bug (shared time accessors trimmed more than once) produced files that passed every JSON check but made AnimationMixer.update loop forever in the browser.

Rapier KinematicCharacterController autostep does not engage when the per-step desired horizontal movement is small (about 0.027 m at 60 Hz walking); test step climbing at walking speed, not only at run speed.

A headless system Chrome driven over the DevTools protocol, using the production build and software GL, gives real end-to-end evidence without a browser tool (it found a hang a unit test missed); use Debugger.pause or a process sample when the page hangs, and never treat software-GL frame rate as a performance measurement.

@react-three/rapier 1.5.0 hands out useRapier().world as a lazy singleton Proxy and frees it in the provider's unmount effect; any game cleanup that touches the world must run before provider unmount or tolerate a released world.
Adding a peer-constrained devDependency can force a bump of an unrelated pinned package (here @types/node ^20 to ^22); run the install early and record such bumps.

measuredClipSpeeds.method: Node forward kinematics of the unmodified source clips (30 fps) with @gltf-transform/core and three math; stance frames chosen from world-space foot height and speed. Not a browser foot-contact check.

walk.plantedFootWorldSpeedMedianMps: 0.017 left, 0.020 right (confirms root-motion speed equals ground speed)
walk.hipsDroppedStanceFootBackwardSpeedMps: 0.949 mean (left 0.801, right 1.090); this is the shipped condition

run.pelvisHeadingDeg: min 15.7, mean 30.0, max 51.9 (mean equals the path heading, so legs swing along the pelvis forward axis, which is why dropping Hips rotation is expected to read as forward running)
run.hipsDroppedStanceFootBackwardSpeedMps: 2.840 mean (left 2.811, right 2.869); this is the shipped condition

measuredClipSpeeds.visualNote: In one automated side-view capture the run read as a forward run with a lean (not sideways); this is a single frame under software GL and R2 stays a QA visual check.

r1Decision.decision: tuned walk and run speeds toward the clips, kept the timeScale clamp
r1Decision.alternativeNotTaken: spec defaults 2.2 and 4.8 would need rates 2.2 and 1.6 for walk/run vs clamp 1.8; a faster Mixamo walk clip would allow a higher walk speed (owner action)

A2.evidence: useRapier().world is not the raw RAPIER.World but a lazy singleton Proxy over it: node_modules/@react-three/rapier/dist/react-three-rapier.esm.js:604-626 (createSingletonProxy) and :711 (useConst(() => createSingletonProxy(() => new rapier.World(...)))); typed as World at declarations/src/components/Physics.d.ts:79. Method calls through the proxy work (the production browser run steps and queries the world through it). Hazard: the provider frees the world in its unmount effect, then resets the proxy (esm.js:712-717), so a later access silently creates a brand new World. paused only skips the library's own step callback: esm.js:972-975 (if (!paused) step(delta)); prop declared at Physics.d.ts:239. The game never relies on library stepping.
A2.consequence: motor.dispose and collider removal are try/catch tolerant of a released world; the shell disposes the game handle before the scene unmounts.

A3.verdict: confirmed for names, corrected for autostep behavior
A3.evidence: node_modules/@dimforge/rapier3d-compat/control/character_controller.d.ts: setUp:49, setApplyImpulsesToDynamicBodies:51, setSlideEnabled:90, enableAutostep:114 (maxHeight, minWidth, includeDynamicBodies), disableAutostep:118, setMaxSlopeClimbAngle:128, setMinSlopeSlideAngle:138, enableSnapToGround:148, disableSnapToGround:152, computeColliderMovement:168, computedMovement:172, computedGrounded:176; pipeline/world.d.ts createCharacterController:177, removeCharacterController:183. Behavior: enableAutostep does not trigger when the per-step desired horizontal movement is small (raw Rapier experiment: 0.0267 m per step fails, 0.03 works; at walking speed the capsule stalled about 2.5 s creeping up the 0.2 m step). Fixed with STEP_PROBE in player.ts; covered by the step test at walking speed in player.physics.test.ts. Slope limits, snap-to-ground, 0.35 m step blocking and the 30 vs 45 degree ramp all behave as designed in the tests.

A4.evidence: player.physics.test.ts 'world.free() releases a character controller': after world.free(), calling computedGrounded() on the controller throws (its wasm pointer was released). The 20-cycle test creates and frees the world, motor and colliders 20 times and checks characterControllers.size 1 then 0 after motor.dispose, and bodies.len and colliders.len 0 after the collider disposer. Wasm memory growth itself was not measured.

A5.evidence: RAPIER.init() from @dimforge/rapier3d-compat 0.14.0 initializes in Node under Vitest 5.0.3 (first test in player.physics.test.ts passes; all 15 physics tests run on the real engine). Also confirmed in the browser through the production build, whose game chunk bundles the compat build.

steps: In the worktree on Node 22: npm run dev (http://localhost:3000) or npm run build then npm start.
Open http://localhost:3000/ (explicit selector: http://localhost:3000/?arena=test, same arena in M1) in a WebGL-capable Chrome.
Wait for the avatar to load (the hero shows the model); the '[ play / explore ]' button then becomes enabled (it stays disabled while the voice status is connecting, while loading, or without WebGL).

Click '[ play / explore ]': the hero is replaced in the same canvas by TEST_ARENA with a follow camera behind the avatar. Controls: W/A/S/D or arrows move (camera-relative), Shift run, Space jump, drag on the canvas to look, R recenter.

Features to exercise: wall at z=0 (x -10 to -2), ramps 30 and 45 degrees at x -12 and -7 (z from 2), steps 0.2 m (x 0) and 0.35 m (x 5) at z 2 to 4, 1 m ledge at (0, 10), a 4 x 4 m pit at x 8 to 12, z 8 to 12 and the open arena edges (falling below y -10 respawns at the spawn at (0, -12)).
Click '[ exit ]' (top left) to return to the hero.
arenaAccess.headlessProbe: The same sequence was executed against the production build by an automated headless Chrome with software GL (frame rate about 12 fps there; not a performance figure). Real GPU, mobile and visual-quality checks are untested here (no browser tool for interactive review).
